;International relations
*[[2017–18 North Korea crisis]]
**[[April 2018 inter-Korean summit|2018 inter-Korean summit]], [[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
***[[South Korea]] states that they want high-level talks with [[North Korea]] before the summit. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-missiles/south-korea-aims-for-high-level-talks-about-talks-with-north-idUSKCN1GS0B0 (Reuters)]
**[[South Korea–United States relations]]
***South Korea and the [[United States]] announce that the [[Foal Eagle]] and [[Key Resolve]] military drills will be scaled down and shortened.  [http://themalaymailonline.com/world/article/report-s.-korea-us-to-scale-down-military-drills (''The Malay Mail'')]
*[[Crime in the United Kingdom]], [[Russia–United Kingdom relations]]
**The death of [[Russia]]n businessman [[Nikolai Glushkov]], who lived in exile in the [[United Kingdom]], is confirmed by a coroner's examination to be a murder. The killing happened eight days after the [[poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-43433552 (''BBC'')]

;Law and crime
*[[South African Arms Deal]]
**[[South Africa]]'s [[National Prosecuting Authority]] Director [[Shaun Abrahams]] says former [[President of South Africa|President]] [[Jacob Zuma]] will be prosecuted for corruption, relating to a [[South African rand|R]]30 billion arms deal in the late 1990s. Zuma disputes all the allegations against him. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/mar/16/south-africa-reinstates-corruption-charges-jacob-zuma (''The Guardian'')]
*[[The Holocaust in Latvia]]
**Police arrest a man at the [[Freedom Monument]] displaying a poster of [[Einsatzgruppen|soldiers killing Jews]] as a protest against an annual march in [[Riga]], [[Latvia]], honoring two [[Latvian Legion|Latvian SS divisions]] during [[World War II]]. [https://www.jta.org/2018/03/16/news-opinion/hundreds-accompany-ss-veterans-march-latvia (JTA)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/in-latvia-hundreds-march-in-honor-of-ss-veterans/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[Aviation in the United States]]
**The [[Federal Aviation Administration]] of the United States restricts "doors off" aircraft flights following a [[2018 New York City Eurocopter AS350 crash|helicopter crash that killed 5 people]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2018/03/16/us/faa-suspends-most-doors-off-flights/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Catholic Church sexual abuse cases]]
**[[Anthony Sablan Apuron]], the former Archbishop of the [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Agaña]], [[Guam]] is found guilty on charges of the sexual abuse of minors by a tribunal. He is suspended from the exercise of his authority over the archdiocese. [https://zenit.org/articles/apostolic-tribunal-of-cdf-finds-guam-archbishop-guilty/ (Zenit)]
**Another lawsuit is filed against the [[Catholic Church in Guam]], bringing the total lawsuits alleging historical sexual abuse to 157. [[Louis Brouillard]], who is now 96, was on Guam from 1948 to 1981, and is accused of abusing boys in 100 of the lawsuits the church is facing. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/350833/sex-abuse-claim-against-guam-church-brings-total-lawsuits-to-157 (RNZ)]

;Politics and elections
*[[First presidency of Donald Trump|Presidency of Donald Trump]]
**[[United States Attorney General|U.S. Attorney General]] [[Jeff Sessions]] fires former [[Deputy Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation|Deputy FBI Director]] [[Andrew McCabe]] because of a report from the [[Office of Professional Responsibility]] accusing McCabe of making an unauthorized news media disclosure and lacking candor on multiple occasions. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/andrew-mccabe-fired-before-retires-no-pension-2018-03-16/ (CBS News)]

;Science and technology
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**European astronomers discover eight new [[exoplanet]]s classified as [[Hot Jupiter]]s as part of the [[Wide Angle Search for Planets|WASP]] project. [https://www.thetalkingdemocrat.com/2018/03/8-new-exoplanets-have-been-discovered/ (''The Talking Democrat'')]
